'''Perry Nisen''' is an American [[physician]] and the former chief executive officer ([[CEO]]) of the [[Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute]]  (SBP), and  held the Donald Bren Chief Executive Chair.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sanford Burnham Prebys CEO Perry Nisen Retiring in September|url=https://timesofsandiego.com/tech/2017/08/10/sanford-burnham-prebys-ceo-perry-nisen-retiring-in-september/|website=Times of San Diego|date=2017-08-10}}</ref><ref name =tribune/> 

==Early life and education==
Nisen received his B.S. degree from [[Stanford University]], M.D. and Ph.D. from the [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]], and has been a resident at [[Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons]].<ref name="sbpdiscovery.org">{{cite web|url=https://www.sbpdiscovery.org/team/perry-nisen-md-phd|title=Perry Nisen, M.D., Ph.D. - SBP|website=www.sbpdiscovery.org}}</ref>

==Career==
At one point,{{when|date=April 2025}} he was the Lowe Foundation Professor of Neuro-Oncology at the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]]. He headed a basic research laboratory and was a practicing physician in pediatric [[hematology]]-[[oncology]]. He was a  member of the Genetics and Development Graduate Training Program.<ref name="sbpdiscovery.org"/>

Nisen has worked in [[GlaxoSmithKline|GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)]], holding such positions as interim Chief Medical Officer, Senior Vice President and Oncology Therapy Area Head, Senior Vice President of Cancer Research, and Senior Vice President of Clinical Pharmacology and Discovery Medicine.<ref>{{cite web |title=Perry D. Nisen M.D., Ph.D.: Executive Profile & Biography |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=270538989&privcapId=4339276&previousCapId=277799796&previousTitle=INTELLIA%20THERAPEUTICS%20INC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823020805/https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=270538989&privcapId=4339276&previousCapId=277799796&previousTitle=INTELLIA%20THERAPEUTICS%20INC |archive-date=2017-08-23 |website=Bloomberg}}</ref> At one point,{{when|date=April 2025}} he was appointed as Senior Vice President of Science and Innovation at (GSK), contributing to the discovery, development and commercialization of a number of drugs.<ref name="Nature">{{cite journal|title=Q&A: Perry Nisen|journal=Nature|date=5 November 2015|volume=527|issue=7576|pages=S18|doi=10.1038/527S18a|pmid=26536220|last1=Bender|first1=Eric|last2=Bender|first2=E.|bibcode=2015Natur.527S..18B |doi-access=free}}</ref>

He had been appointed as CEO in August 2014.<ref name =tribune>{{cite news|title=Meet Sanford-Burnham's new CEO Perry Nisen|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/science/sdut-cancer-drugs-sanford-nisen-2014aug19-story.html|agency=San Diego Union Tribune|date=19 August 2014}}</ref>
